summary: Luke Badiali modelled the cost and return of the origination engine with James Whitlow and Sophie Archer. The full engine costs around £210,000 a year including the analyst, CRM, events and content. We agreed it pays back if it lifts proprietary deals and saves about one turn of EBITDA on entry.

discussion.keyPoints: Analyst £55,000 loaded, CRM £18,000, dinners £24,000, report and video £40,000, plus about £73,000 of partner time.
A proprietary deal at 7x rather than 8x on a £5m EBITDA platform saves £5m of entry value.
James questioned whether the 40% proprietary target is realistic in year one.

recommendations.recommendation: Track origination cost per signed heads of terms, with a target below £70,000.
Approve a budget of £210,000 a year for the engine, reviewed at 12 months.
Model three scenarios for year one: 1, 2 or 3 proprietary platforms.
Charge deal sourcing costs to portfolio companies where possible.

actions.action: Take the £210,000 budget to the partners meeting

nextFocus: Review progress against the origination targets in the follow-up session.
nextPreparation: Sophie to bring the 12-week outreach results by sub-sector.

tests.question: What is the target cost per heads of terms?
How many proprietary platforms are in the scenarios?
